objects.definition: class Condition;
objects.description: Forward declaration for a class named Condition within iox::popo. Only declared here; no definition provided in this header.
Strongly-typed enum describing attachment errors for WaitSet operations: the wait set is full, or an object is already attached.

Internal event record stored by Listener. Holds origin pointer, event type identifiers, user type, callback pointers, translation callback, event id, and an invalidation callback. Provides initialization, reset, equality check, and callback execution. Lifetime and behavior are managed by Listener.

Threaded event listener that attaches to event sources and invokes registered callbacks concurrently. Manages an internal thread, condition listener, and a fixed-capacity array of guarded Event_t entries. Construction allowed with default constructor or with a ConditionVariableData via a friend builder. Copy/move disabled. Users attach/detach events with template APIs; capacity is limited to MAX_NUMBER_OF_EVENTS_PER_LISTENER.
Error enum returned by Listener APIs wrapped in expected. Indicates listener capacity reached, duplicate event attachment, or missing callback.

Event-based trigger object for application code to manually signal events to a WaitSet/Listener within iceoryx. It is non-copyable and non-movable, holds an internal TriggerHandle that is managed when attached to a WaitSet. trigger() signals if attached; hasTriggered() reports whether it has fired since last handling. Private methods are for WaitSet integration (enable/disable/invalidate). Details like threading and lifetime are governed by the owning WaitSet/TriggerHandle; specifics are not present in this header.

Configuration struct for iox::popo publishers. Provides history queue capacity, optional node name, whether to offer on creation, and how to handle slow consumers. Offers serialize()/deserialize() to convert to/from a Serialization payload. Some field semantics (e.g., deprecation of nodeName) are implied by comments; details of Serialization and ConsumerTooSlowPolicy are defined elsewhere.

Configuration struct for iox::popo subscribers. Holds queue capacity, history request, node name (deprecated), auto-subscribe flag, queue overflow policy, and a flag requiring publisher history support. Provides serialize/deserialize API to convert options to/from iox::detail::Serialization format. Construction is aggregate; default member initializers establish sensible defaults. No ownership semantics beyond plain value members.

Configuration struct for an iceoryx server endpoint. Holds queue capacity and overflow policies for requests/responses, an optional node name (deprecated), and flags for offering on creation. Provides serialize/deserialize helpers and equality comparison. Construction is by aggregate initialization; no custom constructor is defined here. Some member types (ServerChunkQueueData_t, NodeName_t, QueueFullPolicy, ConsumerTooSlowPolicy, Serialization, expected) are referenced but defined elsewhere.

Configuration struct for an iceoryx client in namespace iox::popo. Holds queue sizes and policies, a deprecated node name, and flags controlling connect behavior. Provides serialize/deserialize and equality comparison. Exact semantics of policies and limits depend on referenced types defined elsewhere. Construction is via aggregate initialization; no special destruction requirements are indicated.

Base RPC header embedded in iceoryx request/response chunks. Stores RPC header version, routing info to the client queue (unique client queue id and last-known index), and a sequence ID used to correlate responses to requests. Provides accessors to the surrounding ChunkHeader and payload. Moveable, non-copyable. Construction requires the client queue id, last-known index, sequence id, and an explicit header version.

RPC request header extending RpcBaseHeader. Constructed with a client queue id and last-known client queue index; sequence id can be set later via setSequenceId. Provides utility to retrieve the header from a user payload pointer.

RPC response header extending RpcBaseHeader. Adds a server error flag with setters/getters and is constructed with client queue id, last-known client queue index, and sequence id. Provides utilities to obtain the header from a payload pointer.

Abstract singleton-like runtime class used by applications to communicate with the RouDi daemon in iceoryx. Provides factory-based initialization, lifetime extension via an RAII ScopeGuard, and virtual methods to create and acquire middleware primitives (publisher, subscriber, client, server, interface ports, condition variable) and to send IPC requests to RouDi. Not copyable or movable; derived implementations must define the pure virtual functions and manage the singleton access via the runtime factory.

Forward-declared test-only interface class in namespace iox::roudi_env. Only a declaration is present in this header; no definition or members are provided here. Purpose is to grant friendship to PoshRuntime for testing hooks.

Concrete runtime class for single-process usage in iceoryx. It derives from PoshRuntimeImpl and likely customizes behavior for scenarios where publishers/subscribers reside within the same process. The header declares a constructor taking a RuntimeName_t and a non-virtual destructor; full behavior is defined elsewhere.
Strongly-typed enum identifying the messaging pattern of a service: publish/subscribe or request/response. Used to filter services in discovery.
Enum for ServiceDiscovery-related events. Currently only signals that the service registry has changed. Underlying type is popo::EventEnumIdentifier.

Runtime helper class that discovers available services and allows querying them based on service/instance/event and the messaging pattern. It subscribes to the RouDi service registry and emits events when the registry changes. Copy/move is disabled; lifetime managed by user. Requires integration with popo waitset/notification for events. Details of RouDi service registry and subscriber behavior are external to this header.

functions.name: iox::popo::Subscriber::~Subscriber
functions.description: Destructor for the templated iox::popo::Subscriber that performs cleanup. On destruction it resets the internal trigger (used for waitset/notification integration) to detach/cleanup notification resources. Usage: implicitly invoked when a Subscriber<T,H> goes out of scope or is deleted. It is noexcept and will not propagate exceptions. Template parameters: T is the user payload type; H is the optional user header type (defaults to mepoo::NoUserHeader).
requirements: Must be called on a valid, fully constructed Subscriber<T,H> instance (implicit when object lifetime ends).
The object must not be used after the destructor has run.
If managed via a pointer, ensure it is deleted exactly once and not from multiple threads concurrently.
No exceptions may escape this destructor (it is declared noexcept).

functions.name: iox::popo::Client::~Client
functions.signature: template <typename Req, typename Res> iox::popo::Client<Req, Res>::~Client() noexcept
functions.description: Destructor for the request-response Client. It performs cleanup by resetting the internal trigger (Impl::m_trigger), ensuring no lingering triggers remain after the client is destroyed. Typical usage is automatic when a Client<Req,Res> object goes out of scope.
requirements: Object must be a valid instance of iox::popo::Client<Req, Res> at destruction time.
No exceptions are thrown by this destructor (noexcept).

functions.name: iox::popo::Client::Client
functions.signature: template <typename Req, typename Res> explicit iox::popo::Client<Req, Res>::Client(typename iox::popo::ClientImpl<Req, Res>::PortType&& port) noexcept
functions.description: Private constructor that creates a Client by moving in a ClientImpl<Req,Res>::PortType and forwarding it to the base ClientImpl. Intended to be called by the friend builder (iox::posh::experimental::ClientBuilder) to construct a Client with an already-initialized port.
requirements: This constructor is private; only iox::posh::experimental::ClientBuilder (declared as friend) may call it.
Argument port must be an rvalue of type ClientImpl<Req, Res>::PortType.
Construction is noexcept; callers must not rely on exceptions for error handling.

functions.name: iox::popo::Server::~Server
functions.signature:
template <typename Req, typename Res>
iox::popo::Server<Req, Res>::~Server() noexcept
functions.description: Destructor for the templated Server used in iceoryx request-response communication. On destruction it resets the underlying trigger from the ServerImpl base (Impl::m_trigger.reset()), releasing any associated trigger resources. Use in normal object lifetime management to cleanly tear down a Server instance. No exceptions are thrown due to noexcept.
requirements: Must be invoked only once per object lifetime (standard C++ destruction rule).
Object must be a valid, fully constructed iox::popo::Server<Req, Res> instance at the time of destruction.
Do not access the Server instance after the destructor has begun or completed (object is no longer valid).

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::WaitSet
functions.description: Constructs a WaitSet that can attach up to CAPACITY triggers (events/states) and acquires a condition variable from RouDi. The condition variable’s lifetime is bound to the WaitSet’s lifetime. Instances are non-movable and non-copyable.
requirements: No explicit runtime or ownership requirements are documented for construction.
Resulting object must not be moved or copied (class disables copy/move).
CAPACITY equals the template argument; attachments beyond CAPACITY will fail when attaching.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::~WaitSet
functions.description: Destroys the WaitSet and releases the associated condition variable back to the system (RouDi). Any outstanding waits are unblocked by prior markForDestruction or normal teardown.
requirements: The WaitSet should not be used after destruction.
No additional explicit requirements are documented.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::markForDestruction
functions.description: Marks the WaitSet for destruction and wakes any thread currently blocked in wait() or timedWait(). After this call, wait() and timedWait() do not block and never return triggered events/states.
requirements: Call only on a valid (not yet destroyed) WaitSet instance.
After calling, do not rely on wait()/timedWait() to block or to return notifications.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::attachEvent
functions.description: Attaches a specific event (selected by eventType) from eventOrigin to the WaitSet, optionally tagging it with a user-defined notificationId and an optional callback. The WaitSet does not take ownership of the callback or any optional context data.
requirements: EventType must be an enum type (enforced by enable_if).
eventOrigin must remain valid for as long as the event is attached.
The eventCallback and any referenced context data must outlive the attachment (no ownership is taken).
At most CAPACITY total attachments can be present; otherwise returns WaitSetError::WAIT_SET_FULL.
Attaching an already attached event results in WaitSetError::ALREADY_ATTACHED.
notificationId is a user-defined 64-bit value; its meaning is user-defined.
eventType must be a valid event specifier for the type T (per T’s interface).

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::attachState
functions.description: Attaches a specific state (selected by stateType) from stateOrigin to the WaitSet, optionally with a user-defined id and callback. The WaitSet does not take ownership of the callback or any optional context data.
requirements: StateType must be an enum type (enforced by enable_if).
stateOrigin must remain valid for as long as the state is attached.
The stateCallback and any referenced context data must outlive the attachment.
Total attachments cannot exceed CAPACITY (WAIT_SET_FULL on overflow).
Attaching an already attached state yields ALREADY_ATTACHED.
id is a user-defined 64-bit value; its meaning is user-defined.
stateType must be valid for T.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::detachEvent
functions.signature:
template <uint64_t Capacity, typename T, typename... Targs>
void iox::popo::WaitSet<Capacity>::detachEvent(T& eventOrigin, const Targs&... args) noexcept
functions.description: Detaches an event-based trigger associated with eventOrigin from the WaitSet. Additional arguments help identify the specific event to detach, as defined by the event origin’s interface.
requirements: eventOrigin must refer to the same object whose event was attached.
args... must match the event-identifying parameters used when attaching (as required by T’s interface).
Safe usage requires that the event was previously attached; behavior if not attached is not specified.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::detachState
functions.signature:
template <uint64_t Capacity, typename T, typename... Targs>
void iox::popo::WaitSet<Capacity>::detachState(T& stateOrigin, const Targs&... args) noexcept
functions.description: Detaches a state-based trigger associated with stateOrigin from the WaitSet. Additional arguments help identify the specific state to detach, as defined by the state origin’s interface.
requirements: stateOrigin must refer to the same object whose state was attached.
args... must match the state-identifying parameters used when attaching (as required by T’s interface).
Safe usage requires that the state was previously attached; behavior if not attached is not specified.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::timedWait
functions.signature:
template <uint64_t Capacity>
typename iox::popo::WaitSet<Capacity>::NotificationInfoVector iox::popo::WaitSet<Capacity>::timedWait(const iox::units::Duration timeout) noexcept
functions.description: Blocks until at least one attached trigger fires or until timeout elapses, then returns a vector of pointers to the triggered NotificationInfo objects.
requirements: timeout specifies the maximum blocking time; exact constraints on negative/zero durations are not documented.
After markForDestruction(), timedWait() will not block and will not return triggered notifications.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::wait
functions.description: Blocks until at least one attached trigger fires and returns a vector of pointers to the triggered NotificationInfo objects.
requirements: After markForDestruction(), wait() will not block and will not return triggered notifications.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::size
functions.signature:
template <uint64_t Capacity>
uint64_t iox::popo::WaitSet<Capacity>::size() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the number of currently attached triggers (events and states) in the WaitSet.
requirements: No additional explicit requirements are documented.

functions.name: iox::popo::WaitSet::capacity
functions.signature:
template <uint64_t Capacity>
static constexpr uint64_t iox::popo::WaitSet<Capacity>::capacity() noexcept
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of triggers that can be attached to this WaitSet instance (CAPACITY).
requirements: No additional explicit requirements are documented.

functions.name: iox::popo::internal::Event_t::~Event_t
functions.description: Destructor for the internal event holder used by Listener to manage a registered event and its callbacks. Cleans up internal state; no exceptions are thrown.

functions.name: iox::popo::internal::Event_t::isEqualTo
functions.signature: bool iox::popo::internal::Event_t::isEqualTo(const void* const origin, const uint64_t eventType, const uint64_t eventTypeHash) const noexcept
functions.description: Checks whether this Event_t matches the given origin and event type identifiers. Useful for detecting duplicates or for detaching a specific event.
requirements: origin is expected to reference the same object that was used when the event was initialized.
Function is noexcept; callers must not rely on exceptions for error handling.

functions.name: iox::popo::internal::Event_t::reset
functions.description: Resets the Event_t to an uninitialized state, releasing the association with any origin, callbacks, and identifiers. Returns whether the reset was successful.
requirements: Function is noexcept; callers must handle the boolean return value to determine success.

functions.name: iox::popo::internal::Event_t::init
functions.signature: void iox::popo::internal::Event_t::init(const uint64_t eventId, void* const origin, void* const userType, const uint64_t eventType, const uint64_t eventTypeHash, iox::popo::internal::GenericCallbackRef_t callback, iox::popo::internal::TranslationCallbackRef_t translationCallback, const iox::function<void(uint64_t)> invalidationCallback) noexcept
functions.description: Initializes the Event_t with identifiers, the event origin, user type/context pointer, and the callbacks used to translate and invoke the user-provided notification. Prepares the event for dispatch by Listener.
requirements: Must be called before executeCallback or matching/detach operations that assume initialization.
callback must reference a valid callable target for the lifetime of the event (inferred from purpose).
translationCallback must reference a valid callable target for the lifetime of the event (inferred from purpose).
invalidationCallback must be callable; it is stored and later invoked with the event id (inferred from parameter type).
Function is noexcept; callers must not expect exceptions.

functions.name: iox::popo::internal::Event_t::executeCallback
functions.description: Invokes the stored callback for this event. Intended to be called by the Listener thread when the corresponding event is triggered.
requirements: Event_t must have been successfully initialized via init before calling executeCallback (inferred from semantics).
Function is noexcept; any internal failure will not throw.

functions.name: iox::popo::internal::Event_t::isInitialized
functions.description: Reports whether this Event_t has been initialized with a valid origin, identifiers, and callbacks.
requirements: No special preconditions. Use return value to guard operations like executeCallback.

functions.name: iox::popo::Listener::Listener
functions.description: Default constructor for a Listener, which reacts to registered events by executing callbacks concurrently in an internal thread. The Listener is thread-safe.
requirements: No construction-time arguments required.
Subsequent attachEvent/detachEvent calls may be made concurrently from any thread.

functions.name: iox::popo::Listener::~Listener
functions.description: Destructor that stops the internal thread and cleans up registered events. No exceptions are thrown.
requirements: After destruction, no further callbacks will be executed.
Ensure that any user-provided callback/context referenced by attached events is no longer needed.

functions.name: iox::popo::Listener::attachEvent
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename EventType, typename ContextDataType, typename = std::enable_if_t<std::is_enum<EventType>::value>> iox::expected<void, iox::popo::ListenerError> iox::popo::Listener::attachEvent(T& eventOrigin, const EventType eventType, const iox::popo::NotificationCallback<T, ContextDataType>& eventCallback) noexcept
functions.description: Attaches an event defined by the origin object T and an enum EventType, associating it with a notification callback to be executed concurrently when the event occurs. Returns an expected with ListenerError on failure.
requirements: May be called concurrently from any thread.
EventType must be an enum type (enforced via SFINAE).
eventCallback must be created with iox::popo::createNotificationCallback (as documented).
attachEvent does not take ownership of the callback or optional context data; both must outlive the attachment.
Check the returned expected for errors; possible ListenerError values include LISTENER_FULL, EVENT_ALREADY_ATTACHED, EMPTY_EVENT_CALLBACK.
Function is noexcept; errors are reported via the expected return, not exceptions.

functions.name: iox::popo::Listener::detachEvent
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename EventType, typename = std::enable_if_t<std::is_enum<EventType>::value>> void iox::popo::Listener::detachEvent(T& eventOrigin, const EventType eventType) noexcept
functions.description: Detaches a previously attached event identified by the origin object and enum EventType. Thread-safe and callable from any thread.
requirements: May be called concurrently from any thread.
EventType must be an enum type (enforced via SFINAE).
Be aware of the documented race condition when detaching the same event from multiple threads and reattaching concurrently; best practice is to detach a specific event only from one thread.
Function is noexcept; no exceptions will be thrown.

functions.name: iox::popo::Listener::capacity
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of events that can be attached to this Listener.
requirements: No preconditions. Callable without an instance.

functions.name: iox::popo::Listener::size
functions.description: Returns the current number of events attached to this Listener.
requirements: No preconditions. Use return value to check occupancy against capacity().

functions.name: iox::popo::UserTrigger::UserTrigger
functions.description: Default-constructs a UserTrigger that can be attached to a WaitSet/Listener to emit an application-defined event. Use this to create a trigger object; it has no effect until attached by the framework (via WaitSet/Listener). No side effects and guaranteed not to throw.
requirements: Object must subsequently be attached to a WaitSet/Listener (by the framework) for triggering to have any effect.
Do not copy or move this type; copy/move constructors and assignments are deleted.

functions.name: iox::popo::UserTrigger::trigger
functions.description: Signals the user-defined event. If the UserTrigger is attached to a WaitSet/Listener, this will wake/notify it; otherwise, it performs no action. Intended for application code to manually trigger an event.
requirements: Calling when not attached to a WaitSet/Listener is a no-op (no notification will occur).
May be called multiple times; behavior is to signal the attached WaitSet/Listener if attached. Further details about coalescing or edge/level semantics are unknown from this header.
Must be called on a valid, initialized UserTrigger instance.

functions.name: iox::popo::UserTrigger::hasTriggered
functions.description: Queries whether this UserTrigger has been triggered. Returns true if a trigger has occurred and not yet been handled by a WaitSet/Listener, otherwise false. Note: the triggered state is reset after it has been handled by a WaitSet/Listener.
requirements: The triggered state may be reset after handling by a WaitSet/Listener; consumers should account for this when polling.
Must be called on a valid, initialized UserTrigger instance.
No explicit synchronization guarantees are stated; thread-safety is unknown from this header.

functions.name: iox::popo::PublisherOptions::serialize
functions.description: Serializes this PublisherOptions instance into a compact Serialization object. Intended for persisting or transmitting configuration data and later reconstructing it via deserialize. No exceptions are thrown (noexcept). Details of the binary/text format are defined by the Serialization type and are not exposed here.
requirements: The PublisherOptions instance must be in a valid, initialized state before calling serialize.
No exceptions are thrown by this function (noexcept).
Thread-safety and reentrancy guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: iox::popo::PublisherOptions::deserialize
functions.signature: static expected<PublisherOptions, Serialization::Error> deserialize(const Serialization& serialized) noexcept;
functions.description: Deserializes a PublisherOptions object from the provided serialized representation. Returns an expected that contains either a fully reconstructed PublisherOptions on success or a Serialization::Error on failure. No exceptions are thrown (noexcept). Use this to restore PublisherOptions that were previously produced by serialize.
requirements: The 'serialized' parameter must contain a valid PublisherOptions encoding produced by serialize or a compatible format/version.
Caller must check the returned expected for success before using the resulting PublisherOptions and handle the error case (Serialization::Error) appropriately.
No exceptions are thrown by this function (noexcept).
Versioning/compatibility rules of the Serialization format are not specified here; callers should assume mismatched or corrupted input yields an error.

functions.name: iox::popo::SubscriberOptions::serialize
functions.description: Serializes the current SubscriberOptions into an iox::Serialization payload suitable for storage or transport. Typical usage is to persist or transmit configuration and later reconstruct it via deserialize(). The function is noexcept and does not allocate or throw by contract (implementation not shown).
requirements: The SubscriberOptions instance must be a valid, initialized object.
Callers should treat the returned iox::Serialization as opaque and only deserialize it using the corresponding deserialize() for SubscriberOptions.
No exceptions are thrown; callers must not rely on exception-based error handling.

functions.name: iox::popo::SubscriberOptions::deserialize
functions.description: Deserializes a SubscriberOptions object from the provided iox::Serialization blob. Use this to reconstruct options previously produced by SubscriberOptions::serialize(). Returns an expected that contains either a valid SubscriberOptions on success or a Serialization::Error on failure; the function is noexcept.
requirements: The input parameter 'serialized' must contain a valid encoding produced by SubscriberOptions::serialize().
Callers must check the returned iox::expected for success before using the value; on failure, handle the contained iox::Serialization::Error.
No exceptions are thrown; callers must use the error state of the returned expected for error handling.
Behavior is unspecified if 'serialized' was constructed from incompatible versions or different types.

functions.name: iox::popo::ServerOptions::serialize
functions.description: Serializes the current ServerOptions instance into a compact Serialization object for transport or storage. Typical usage is to persist or transmit configuration and later reconstruct it via deserialize. No allocation or throwing is implied by noexcept. The exact serialized layout is defined by the Serialization utility and may change across versions.
requirements: The ServerOptions instance must be properly constructed before calling serialize.
Callers must treat the returned Serialization as opaque and only pass it to compatible deserialization routines (e.g., ServerOptions::deserialize).
No exceptions will be thrown; callers must not rely on exception-based error handling for serialization.

functions.name: iox::popo::ServerOptions::deserialize
functions.signature: static expected<ServerOptions, Serialization::Error> deserialize(const Serialization& serialized) noexcept;
functions.description: Reconstructs a ServerOptions instance from a previously produced Serialization blob. Returns an expected carrying either a valid ServerOptions on success or a Serialization::Error on failure. Intended to be paired with ServerOptions::serialize when transporting or persisting server configuration.
requirements: The input 'serialized' must represent a ServerOptions produced by a compatible version of ServerOptions::serialize; malformed or incompatible data will cause an error result.
Callers must check the returned expected for success before using the contained ServerOptions and handle the error case (Serialization::Error) appropriately.
No exceptions will be thrown due to noexcept; all failures are reported via the expected error value.
The function does not modify the input 'serialized'.

functions.name: iox::popo::ServerOptions::operator==
functions.signature: bool operator==(const ServerOptions& rhs) const noexcept;
functions.description: Compares this ServerOptions with another for equality. Returns true if all relevant configuration fields are equal, false otherwise. Useful for testing or detecting configuration changes. No exceptions are thrown.
requirements: Both the current object and 'rhs' must be valid ServerOptions instances.
Comparison is a pure operation with no side effects and is noexcept; callers must not rely on exceptions.

functions.name: iox::popo::ClientOptions::serialize
functions.description: Serializes this ClientOptions instance into a compact iox::Serialization object for persistence or IPC transport. Typical usage is to capture the current option values and later reconstruct them via deserialize. No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).
requirements: The ClientOptions instance must be a valid, initialized object.
Caller should assume the produced serialization is only intended to be consumed by ClientOptions::deserialize of a compatible library version.
Caller must not expect exceptions; errors are not reported by this function.

functions.name: iox::popo::ClientOptions::deserialize
functions.signature: static iox::expected<iox::popo::ClientOptions, iox::Serialization::Error> iox::popo::ClientOptions::deserialize(const iox::Serialization& serialized) noexcept
functions.description: Deserializes a ClientOptions instance from the provided iox::Serialization blob. Returns an iox::expected that contains either a reconstructed ClientOptions on success or a Serialization::Error on failure. Use this to restore options previously created by serialize. No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).
requirements: The input parameter 'serialized' must contain a valid serialization compatible with ClientOptions (ideally produced by ClientOptions::serialize).
Caller must check the returned iox::expected and handle the error case (Serialization::Error) appropriately; no exceptions will be thrown.
The function may fail if the serialization format/version or content is incompatible or malformed.

functions.name: iox::popo::ClientOptions::operator==
functions.description: Compares this ClientOptions with another for equality. Intended to test whether two configurations are identical across all option fields. No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).
requirements: The right-hand side parameter 'rhs' must be a valid, initialized ClientOptions object.

functions.name: iox::popo::RpcBaseHeader::RpcBaseHeader

functions.description: Constructs and initializes the RPC base header for an iceoryx request/response chunk. functions.name: iox::runtime::ServiceDiscovery::findService
functions.signature: void iox::runtime::ServiceDiscovery::findService(const iox::optional<capro::IdString_t>& service, const iox::optional<capro::IdString_t>& instance, const iox::optional<capro::IdString_t>& event, const iox::function_ref<void(const capro::ServiceDescription&)> callableForEach, const iox::popo::MessagingPattern pattern) noexcept
functions.description: Searches the service registry for all services matching the provided service/instance/event identifiers and messaging pattern, and invokes the provided callback for each match. Passing nullopt for service, instance, or event acts as a wildcard for that field. Supported messaging patterns include PUB_SUB and REQ_RES. Intended usage: supply any combination of identifiers and a non-throwing callback to process each matching capro::ServiceDescription.
requirements: service, instance, and event may be iox::nullopt to indicate wildcards; if provided, each must contain a valid capro::IdString_t.
callableForEach must be a valid callable with signature void(const capro::ServiceDescription&).
callableForEach must not throw exceptions (the member function is noexcept).
The callback must tolerate being called zero or more times, once per matching service.
Any references or objects captured by callableForEach must remain valid for the duration of the calls.
pattern must be a valid iox::popo::MessagingPattern value (e.g., PUB_SUB or REQ_RES).
This function may be called at any time after construction; additional concurrency or ordering guarantees are not documented.

data_types.description: A string restricted to characters typically safe for filesystem names without path separators: ASCII letters (A–Z, a–z), digits (0–9), underscore (_), hyphen (-), and dot (.). Length may be limited (e.g., truncated to an implementation-defined capacity). Suitable for identifiers that must conform to filename-like constraints.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: filename-safe string used as RuntimeName_t
# Allowed chars: A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - .
# The stub filters arbitrary FUZZ_PARAM_STR through that whitelist and truncates to 80.
# If empty after filtering, it substitutes with "fuzz_app".
# Our goal: produce interesting but valid names that exercise different code paths,
# including boundary lengths and varied character classes. The fuzzer harness will
# take the returned bytes as the initial buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_.-"

# A small corpus of interesting seeds to cover behaviors
CORPUS: List[str] = [
    # minimal valid
    "a",
    # default-fallback trigger would not happen since we provide valid chars; keep one minimal anyway
    # mixed classes
    "App_01",
    "node-xyz",
    "v1.2.3",
    # long near boundary (79 and 80 safe chars)
    "A" * 79,
    "B" * 80,
    # diverse pattern with all classes
    "Abc_123-Name.With.Dots-Under_Score-9",
    # starts with dot or dash (still valid in whitelist)
    ".hidden_name",
    "-dash-prefix",
]

def _rand_safe_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a strategy to get variety
    strategy = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    if strategy == 0:
        # Pick from corpus
        return rng.choice(CORPUS)
    elif strategy == 1:
        # Random short 1..10
        n = rng.randint(1, 10)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    elif strategy == 2:
        # Random medium 20..40
        n = rng.randint(20, 40)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    elif strategy == 3:
        # Boundary near 80: 70..85 (the stub will truncate to 80)
        n = rng.randint(70, 85)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    elif strategy == 4:
        # Construct with repeating classes blocks
        blocks = [
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8))),
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6))),
            '_',
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6))),
            '-',
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8))),
            '.',
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))),
        ]
        s = ''.join(blocks)
        # Ensure not exceeding 80 too much; the stub truncates but we cap to 100
        return s[:100]
    else:
        # Exactly 80 characters with varied segments
        segments = []
        while sum(len(x) for x in segments) < 80:
            choice = rng.randrange(4)
            if choice == 0:
                seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)))
            elif choice == 1:
                seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)))
            elif choice == 2:
                seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)))
            else:
                seg = rng.choice("_.-")
            segments.append(seg)
        s = ''.join(segments)
        return s[:80]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    s = _rand_safe_string(rng)
    # The stub will filter, but we already restrict to safe set to ensure it remains non-empty.
    # Ensure overall size limit (<=4096 bytes)
    b = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    if not b:
        b = b"fuzz_app"
    return b[:4096]
